newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia regrets shooting of Turkish fisherman.
newsitem.headline: Georgia regrets shooting of Turkish fisherman.

text.p: Georgia President Eduard Shevardnadze expressed regret on Friday over the Russian coast guard's fatal shooting of a Turkish fisherman caught in Georgia's Black Sea territorial waters.

The shooting occurred on Wednesday when Russian coastguard cutters, which patrol the area under an agreement with the Georgian government, were sent to intercept nine Turkish vessels spotted in the former Soviet republic's territorial waters.
A Russian coast guard spokesman said all the boats fled except one, which began to execute what he called a dangerous manoeuvre. The coast guard responded by shooting at the "poachers".
"Even fishing a tonne of fish from our territorial waters is not worth the loss of a human life," Shevardnadze told the Turkish ambassador to Georgia, his office said on Friday.
"Unfortunately we have very big problems with Russian border guards. It's already the third case when they have acted without our agreement," he said.
"If I knew about this earlier on, I would have, of course, in no case allowed the violence against an unarmed fisherman," he said. "I am greatly concerned and regret this tragic event."
The Turkish ambassador demanded that Georgia return the ship and its crew now located at the Georgian port of Batumi, base for the Russian coastguards.
He also said Georgia should pay Turkey damages for the moral and material loss from the incident, Shevardnadze's office said.
